by: ENGINE, integration pass (batch 1) — written BEFORE any planner fixture was played in the harness
what: engine/all_mechanics_fire.js plays engine/stage_planner.js fixtures (fixture + one-leaf control, every rendered side/slot variant, the fixture's own arm and HP pool, the sheet's declared spread and gender) instead of its hand-picked bodies
design_that_the_numbers_depend_on: abilities and items: the planner fixture is the FIRST stage; the verdict is the existing A/B (abRow) over the fixture game and its one-leaf control, so a FIRED means what it meant before

a planned row that does not fire, or cannot be staged, falls back LOUDLY to the legacy ladder (stage: legacy-fallback, the planner verdict kept beside it); a row the planner refuses runs legacy with the refusal code. So fired cannot fall below the baseline on a deterministic engine, and every fallback is a planner gap named in the artifact

moves: the legacy consequence ladder stays the primary verdict (it carries leaf_effect and announcement_only, which coverage.js reads), and every move row ALSO plays its planner fixture on every variant; a move the legacy arm cannot resolve takes the planner's resolution
every variant (near, far, slot b where rendered) is played; a board that parts on ANY variant marks the row's board STATE

gender (Attract, Cute Charm, Rivalry) plays through a new opt-in declared-gender seam in engine/game_differential.js buildPair, with medicham2 appending ', M' / ', F' to its switch and detailschange details exactly as sim/pokemon.ts getUpdatedDetails does
every planned row plays its sheet's declared spread (0 SP, Hardy) through a new opt-in declared-spread seam, because the planner judged its speed windows on that sheet
